_provenance.executed_by: External ChatGPT browser run supplied by the operator. This REPLACES the earlier internal Stage 3 pass. factual_accuracy_score 70 reflects the Stage 1/pre-correction draft; all five cardinal-sin flags were integrated in Stage 6 synthesis v3 (see synthesis revisions).

claims.claim: PDPA 2010 (Act 709) Section 3 reads exactly: "This Act shall not apply to the Federal Government and State Governments."
claims.source: Act 709 official PDF pdp.gov.my; JPDP 'Application and Non-Application of the Act' page. Act dated 2 June 2010.
claims.stale_check: Act A1727 did not amend Section 3.

claims.claim: On 30 April 2026 JPDP adopted three guidelines (DPIA, DPbD, ADMP v1.0).
claims.source: Guideline PDFs on pdp.gov.my say each is 'issued' by the Commissioner; JPDP X launch post + reporting place the launch on 30 Apr 2026, but the texts do not display 'adopted on 30 April 2026'.
claims.correction: Safer: 'JPDP published/issued three guidelines in April 2026 and officially launched them on 30 April 2026.'

claims.claim: DPIA mandatory >20,000 data subjects, or >10,000 with sensitive data, OR any ADMP regardless of volume.
claims.source: DPIA Guideline para 7.5 (thresholds); ADMP Guideline para 6.1 (ADMP triggers DPIA regardless of extent), pdp.gov.my.
claims.correction: Volume-independent trigger comes from the ADMP Guideline, not DPIA para 7.5.

claims.claim: On 30 April Malaysia adopted its first rules forcing any firm that profiles you to run an impact check first.
claims.source: ADMP Guideline paras 1.1, 1.2, 6.1; DPIA Guideline, pdp.gov.my.
claims.correction: Avoid claiming the PDFs prove a 30 April 'adoption' date; use 'issued in April 2026 / launched 30 April 2026'.

claims.claim: The one profiler they cannot reach is the government.
claims.source: Section 3 exempts Federal/State Governments; JPDP 2020 PCP states statutory bodies must comply and discusses extending the Act to government.
claims.correction: More precise: Act 709 does not apply to the Federal/State Governments, though statutory bodies are not automatically exempt.

claims.claim: PADU, the state database on more than 30 million people, falls outside them.
claims.source: Official PADU material 20 Apr 2026: 30.7 million socioeconomic profiles (padu.gov.my/mediagambar/20-04-2026-hala-tuju-padu.pdf); Act 709 s.3.
claims.stale_check: 30.7 million as of 20 Apr 2026; 'more than 30 million' safe.

claims.claim: PADU holds more than 30 million people on 600+ data points.
claims.source: 30.7m verified (official PADU 20 Apr 2026). No retrievable PADU/Economy Ministry primary document found for the '600+' data-point figure; only secondary reporting.
claims.correction: Publish 30.7m as the verified figure; drop or attribute '600+ data points' to secondary reporting.

claims.claim: 22.5 million Malaysians' MyKad details put up for sale in 2022.
claims.source: JPN clipping archive (19 May 2022); Bernama/Astro Awani 18 May 2022 (22.5 million).

claims.claim: ...no one had recourse under the data-protection law against any government agency (tied to 2022).
claims.source: Act 709 s.3; JPDP FAQ (Act 709 remedies are complaint/criminal, no specific damages right); minister denied NRD was the source.
claims.correction: Legal point sound in the abstract; tying it to the 2022 incident is misleading unless a government agency is first established as the cause.

claims.claim: The minister denied it came from the registration department.
claims.source: Bernama via Astro Awani 18 May 2022 (Hamzah Zainudin); JPN clipping 'Penjualan Data Bukan Milik JPN' 19 May 2022.

claims.claim: Any firm that profiles people by machine must now file an impact assessment, even on one person.
claims.source: ADMP Guideline para 6.1 (DPIA required regardless of extent). No primary requirement found to file/submit every DPIA to the Commissioner.
claims.correction: Replace 'file an impact assessment' with 'carry out a DPIA'. Volume-independent part is supportable; the filing part is not.

claims.claim: The assessment is mandatory above 20,000 people, or 10,000 with sensitive data. PADU clears every threshold; the Act that sets them cannot bind it.
claims.source: DPIA Guideline para 7.5; PADU 30.7m (20 Apr 2026); Act 709 s.3.
claims.correction: PADU's 30.7m scale alone clears the >20,000 threshold; no need to imply sensitive-data/ADMP conditions separately established for PADU.

claims.claim: A proposal to delete Section 3 was rejected.
claims.source: JPDP 2020 PCP item 12 considered extending Act 709 to Federal/State Governments; Act A1727 left s.3 untouched. No Cabinet minute/Hansard found proving a formal rejection.
claims.correction: Publish only what is proven: 'JPDP's 2020 consultation considered extending the Act to government, but the 2024 amendment did not remove Section 3.'

claims.source: Act A1727 (gazetted 17 Oct 2024) does not amend s.3; current Act 709 text retains s.3; commencement via P.U.(B) 522 (24 Dec 2024).

claims.claim: Singapore exempts its public sector too, then governs it by a separate 2018 law with criminal penalties for officers.
claims.source: Singapore PDPA s.4 (public-agency exclusion); PSGA 2018 ss.7-8 (offences); PDPC complaint page routes government concerns to PSGA-era channels.

claims.claim: Malaysia passed no equivalent public-sector data-protection statute granting data-subject rights.
claims.source: AGC portal + JPDP materials reviewed; no dedicated public-sector personal-data statute granting data-subject rights against Federal/State Governments located. Absence claim, not verifiable to positive-statute standard.
claims.correction: Safer: 'I did not locate an equivalent Malaysian public-sector data-protection statute granting data-subject rights in the materials reviewed.'
claims.stale_check: Absence claims can become stale; searched 2026-06-06.

claims.claim: The rules rest on a 2010 law that exempts the Federal and State Governments, on the basis it governs commercial dealings.
claims.source: Act 709 applies to processing in connection with commercial transactions; s.3 exempts the Federal/State Governments. The statute does not itself state the exemption exists 'because' the Act governs commercial dealings.
claims.correction: Write as two separate verified facts, not a causal explanation (or attribute the rationale to the minister).

claims.claim: Malaysia... exempted the algorithms that decide who gets help, who gets watched, and who gets missed.
claims.source: Private-sector rulemaking + government exemption verified; no primary documentation located identifying specific Malaysian government algorithmic systems described this way.
claims.correction: Treat as opinion; if retained, identify and source the specific government systems alleged.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: Any firm... must now file an impact assessment, even on one person.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: JPDP texts support carrying out a DPIA regardless of extent, but no primary basis for a blanket duty to file/submit it to the regulator.
cardinal_sin_flags.primary_source: ADMP Guideline para 6.1; DPIA Guideline, pdp.gov.my

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: When 22.5 million... no one had recourse... against any government agency.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: Ties the s.3 legal point to a 2022 breach whose origin was disputed; minister denied NRD was the source.
cardinal_sin_flags.primary_source: Act 709 s.3; JPN clipping; Astro Awani 18 May 2022

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: PADU holds more than 30 million people on 600+ data points, and is exempt.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: 30m + exemption verified; '600+ data points' not found in a PADU/Economy Ministry primary document.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: a proposal to delete Section 3 was rejected
cardinal_sin_flags.why: 2020 consultation considered extension and A1727 left s.3 untouched, but no official record of a formal rejection found.

cardinal_sin_flags.claim: The one profiler they cannot reach is the government.
cardinal_sin_flags.why: s.3 exempts Federal/State Governments, but statutory bodies do comply; 'the government' blurs that distinction.

omitted_facts: JPDP's 2020 PCP expressly considered extending Act 709 to the Federal/State Governments and stated statutory bodies already comply (stronger primary context than the secondary FMT account).
Act A1727 commenced in staggered phases (1 Jan 2025, 1 Apr 2025, 1 Jun 2025) per Gazette P.U.(B) 522 (24 Dec 2024).
JPDP FAQ: Act 709 does not specifically provide a right to claim damages; remedies are framed as criminal offences — materially affects 'recourse' framing.
Official PADU material (20 Apr 2026): 30.7m profiles AND 26 agencies approved (Jan-Mar 2026) to use PADU for decision-making/analytics.
Singapore PDPC routes government-agency data concerns to a Quality Service Manager / Government Data Incident Reporting Platform, not the private-sector PDPA route.
source_assessment: Reasonably broad mix of official regulator/government materials, named news outlets, a bar statement, a Singapore statute, and law-firm explainers. Strongest sourcing: the Malaysian legal framework and 2026 JPDP guidelines. Weakest: the 600+ PADU data-point figure, the alleged Cabinet-level rejection of deleting s.3, and the exact 'adopted on 30 April 2026' wording. The prior T4A issue used as S9b is circular and should not be used for verification. Diversity moderate (regulator/government/business-press facing; lacks parliamentary records, academic analysis, rights-group submissions).
overall_assessment: Core thesis substantially right: Act 709 exempts the Federal/State Governments; JPDP issued ADMP/DPIA/DPbD guidance in April 2026; the framework imposes private-sector obligations that do not bind government under s.3. Not publication-ready without corrections: overstates a requirement ('file' vs 'carry out' a DPIA), relies on non-primary support for the 600+ figure and the s.3-deletion rejection, and uses framing implying government culpability/universality more strongly than the verified record supports. With those tightened, the central argument is factually defensible.
